candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the JSON document body (a run of nested array-start tokens followed by one scalar and the matching array-end tokens) delivered to any ObjectMapper.readValue / readTree / data-binding entry point whose target type is a primitive-typed value (int, long, boolean, byte, short, float, double) or java.util.Date, including primitive-typed POJO properties and primitive collection/map elements. Recursion depth is directly proportional to the attacker-chosen nesting depth; API calls using the vulnerable helpers are reachable from the normal public deserialization API (e.g. readValue(String, Integer.TYPE) resolves to NumberDeserializers.IntegerDeserializer.primitiveInstance, whose deserialize() calls _parseIntPrimitive for the primitive case at NumberDeserializers.java:524-531).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed that equivalent guards exist elsewhere, so this is an omission in the primitive helpers rather than intended behavior: StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue (355-368) rejects a nested START_ARRAY and is called by StdDeserializer._deserializeFromArray (215); BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray has an explicit deeply-nested-array guard (BeanDeserializer.java:631-640, comment dated 23-Aug-2022). Verified that wrapper-type deserializers (Integer, Boolean, Byte, Short, Long, Float, Double, Character, BigInteger, Number) route through _deserializeFromArray (NumberDeserializers.java:300, 391-392, 482, 630, 726-727, 815-816, 943-944), so they are not affected, which narrows the issue to primitive-typed targets. Verified UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is disabled by default (DeserializationFeature.java:326) and that its Javadoc only promises that a single wrapper array is allowed (315-326) - behavior the primitive helpers do not fully enforce. No test sources or git metadata are present in the snapshot, so I could not inspect the upstream fix commit or reproduce the failure; the mapping to a specific publicly tracked deep-nesting DoS advisory is an inference from the code, not a verified fact.
candidates.impact: Denial of service / resource exhaustion in any application that enables UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS and deserializes untrusted JSON into primitive-typed targets: StackOverflowError aborts the request-handling thread and can destabilize the process or degrade availability (repeated requests exhaust worker threads). No confidentiality/integrity impact and no code execution is demonstrated; impact is availability only.
candidates.prerequisites: (1) DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS must be enabled on the ObjectMapper (it is disabled by default, DeserializationFeature.java:326, but is commonly enabled by applications that accept single-element arrays for scalar values). (2) The declared target (root value, bean property, or container element) must be a primitive Java type or java.util.Date so that the _parse*Primitive / _parseDateFromArray helpers are used; wrapper types (Integer, Boolean, ...) go through _deserializeFromArray/_deserializeWrappedValue and are blocked at depth 1. (3) A JSON document with enough nesting to exhaust the default thread stack (a payload of modest size, tens of kilobytes of '[' characters, is typically sufficient); no other privileges or server state are required.
candidates.root_cause: Non-primitive value types unwrap single-element arrays through StdDeserializer._deserializeFromArray(), which delegates to StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue() (lines 347-369) where a nested START_ARRAY is explicitly rejected ("nested Arrays not allowed with UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS"), and BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray() contains an explicit deeply-nested-array guard (BeanDeserializer.java:631-640, comment dated 23-Aug-2022). The primitive-value parse helpers bypass both: when the current token is START_ARRAY and UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled they call p.nextToken() and then immediately re-invoke themselves, without checking whether the element token is again START_ARRAY: _parseBooleanPrimitive (StdDeserializer.java:413-420), _parseBytePrimitive (582-589), _parseShortPrimitive (652-659), _parseIntPrimitive (720-726), _parseLongPrimitive (871-877), _parseFloatPrimitive (1004-1010), _parseDoublePrimitive (1133-1139), and _parseDateFromArray/_parseDate for java.util.Date (1288-1289, 1298-1322). Each nesting level adds one Java stack frame, so an attacker-chosen nesting depth exhausts the thread stack; _verifyEndArrayForSingle (2112) runs only after the recursive call returns and therefore cannot bound the recursion.
candidates.title: Unbounded recursive wrapper-array unwrapping in StdDeserializer primitive-value helpers -> StackOverflowError DoS
candidates.trace: readValue("[[[...scalar...]]]", Integer.TYPE) -> ObjectMapper._readMapAndClose -> DefaultDeserializationContext.readRootValue -> NumberDeserializers.IntegerDeserializer.deserialize (NumberDeserializers.java:524) -> _primitive == true so StdDeserializer._parseIntPrimitive(p, ctxt) is called (StdDeserializer.java:694) -> current token START_ARRAY -> UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS enabled -> p.nextToken(); _parseIntPrimitive(p, ctxt) recursively (720-725); if the next token is still START_ARRAY the switch repeats, adding one stack frame per '[' until StackOverflowError. Identical self-recursion exists in _parseBooleanPrimitive (417), _parseBytePrimitive (586), _parseShortPrimitive (656), _parseLongPrimitive (874), _parseFloatPrimitive (1007), _parseDoublePrimitive (1136); for Date targets, _parseDateFromArray (1315-1317) calls _parseDate whose START_ARRAY branch (1288-1289) re-enters _parseDateFromArray, creating the same unbounded loop. ObjectMapper._readMapAndClose contains no catch (Throwable), and StackOverflowError is an Error (not caught by the usual catch (Exception) handling), so the error escapes the parsing call to the caller.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or crash reproduction was performed; the recursion/StackOverflowError conclusion is based on source reading only. Exact nesting depth needed depends on JVM thread-stack size and on the caller's configuration. Whether a specific deployment enables UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS (the prerequisite) must be checked in that deployment; a custom DeserializationProblemHandler overriding handleUnexpectedToken cannot prevent the stack exhaustion here because the primitive helpers recurse before any error-on-token call is made. Whether this is precisely the issue the benchmark expects, and which upstream commit fixed it, is unconfirmed.

coverage_summary: Scope reported by get_source_scope: 18,045 readable files (no over-size/sensitive/symlink exclusions; binary-like files skipped on read/search). I focused on the 464-file main source tree under src/main/java, using text search across all readable files plus targeted reads of the deserialization stack (deser/, deser/std/, deser/impl/), primitive/array handling (NumberDeserializers, PrimitiveArrayDeserializers), builder/bean deserializers, polymorphic typing (jsontype/, DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator, SubTypeValidator, StdTypeResolverBuilder), configuration defaults (DeserializationFeature, MapperFeature, MapperConfig, ObjectMapper), node/token utilities, and class-loading utilities. The generated docs/javadoc/1.9 tree and attic/ sources were not security-reviewed; no test sources are present in this snapshot, so I could not use repository tests or VCS history to corroborate behavior.
limitations: Static review only: no code was compiled or executed, and no crash was reproduced; the StackOverflowError behavior is inferred from the recursive source paths.
No test sources, release notes, or git/VCS metadata are present in the snapshot, so the upstream fix commit, issue number, and CVE attribution could not be verified.
Generated docs/javadoc/1.9 and attic/ sources were not inspected for vulnerabilities.

Coverage of the large library is necessarily selective: I prioritized deserializer recursion, type-resolution/validator logic, and default configuration; serializer code, annotation/introspection internals, and some util classes were only spot-checked.

Exploitability of the candidate depends on the deployment enabling DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS and using primitive-typed targets; stack size and payload size thresholds were not measured.

rejected_leads.lead: BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray (src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/deser/BuilderBasedDeserializer.java:512-535) lacks the nested-array guard present in BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray (BeanDeserializer.java:631-640). In the unwrap branch it calls deserialize(p, ctxt) at line 529; with a nested START_ARRAY the same method re-enters _deserializeFromArray and recurses unbounded, i.e. the same deep-nesting StackOverflowError for builder-based targets under UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS.
rejected_leads.reason: Same weakness class and same prerequisite as the selected candidate, but narrower reach (requires a builder-based target type and the non-default feature). I could not determine from the snapshot whether the benchmark's fix commit targeted this file or the primitive helpers, and the selected candidate follows the documented 'primitive value deserializers / deep wrapper array nesting' pattern more directly, so this is recorded as a related, unconfirmed lead rather than a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded recursion for deeply nested documents in JsonNodeDeserializer / UntypedObjectDeserializer (JsonNodeDeserializer.java contains an unused ContainerStack with comment 'Not used yet but useful for limits' and a size() accessor but no enforced limit).
rejected_leads.reason: Real stack-overflow exposure in this pre-2.15 snapshot (no StreamReadConstraints/max-nesting-depth exists anywhere in src/main), but it is a general design limitation of the version rather than a single localized missing check, requires no feature flag, and no specific guard/fix could be identified in this snapshot; too broad to submit as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Polymorphic deserialization gadget exposure: ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping() (ObjectMapper.java:2046-2052) uses the configured PolymorphicTypeValidator, and MapperConfig.getPolymorphicTypeValidator (MapperConfig.java:296-305) defaults to LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator unless the application enables MapperFeature.BLOCK_UNSAFE_POLYMORPHIC_BASE_TYPES; SubTypeValidator's blacklist (SubTypeValidator.java:31-120+) is best-effort.
rejected_leads.reason: Well-documented opt-in design in 2.10+ rather than a source defect: exploiting gadgets requires the application to enable default typing with a permissive validator. No concrete bypass in DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator (reviewed, lines 1-119) or other validator code was found, so this is not a defensible single-finding candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: StackTraceElementDeserializer (src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/deser/std/StackTraceElementDeserializer.java:58-62) implements its own UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS handling and recursively calls deserialize(p, ctxt) after p.nextToken() without a nested-array check.
rejected_leads.reason: Same omission pattern but a niche target type (StackTraceElement), reachable only with the feature enabled; not selected because the primitive-value path is broader and more clearly matches the documented deep-wrapper-array threat.

summary: Snapshot is jackson-databind 2.14.0-SNAPSHOT main sources (464 Java files under src/main/java; no tests, no VCS metadata, only generated 1.9 javadoc plus attic/ outside the reviewed scope). I reviewed the deserialization stack (deser/, deser/std/, deser/impl/), polymorphic type handling (jsontype/, cfg/, MapperFeature/MapperConfig), ObjectMapper entry points, node/token helpers and config defaults. One strong candidate emerged: for primitive-typed targets the single-element-array unwrapping helpers in StdDeserializer re-enter themselves after one p.nextToken() without rejecting a nested START_ARRAY, so an attacker-controlled deeply nested JSON array (with DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS enabled) causes unbounded Java recursion and StackOverflowError (resource-exhaustion DoS). The same guard exists on the non-primitive paths (_deserializeWrappedValue, BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray), which is strong counter-context that the primitive helpers are an oversight. Other leads (BuilderBasedDeserializer missing the same guard, unbounded recursion for JsonNode/UntypedObject deep documents, and laissez-faire old-style default typing) were rejected as secondary/unconfirmed. No runtime confirmation is claimed; evidence is static source evidence only.
